Class OAuthTokenService

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.mcp.oauth.OAuthTokenService
@Service @ConditionalOnProperty(prefix="gt.use", name="mcp", havingValue="true") public class OAuthTokenService extends Object
Issues and rotates the tokens of OAuth clients. Every token is a gpat_ token like a personal one and is stored only as its hash, in user_access_token with a reference to its family in oauth_authorization.
  • A code exchange creates the family of the consent; an earlier family of the same user and client is deleted with its tokens, so a new consent replaces the old one.
  • A refresh locks the refresh token and its family, marks the token consumed and issues a new pair. A consumed token presented again is a replay (RFC 9700, section 4.14): the family is revoked and all its tokens are deleted.
  • An access token lives one hour, a refresh token 30 days, neither beyond the end of the family, which lies at most 90 days after the consent.
  • A family is refreshed at most once a minute. Of its consumed refresh tokens the newest 100 stay recognizable; older ones and expired access tokens are deleted in the same transaction as the rotation.

The methods return a OAuthTokenService.TokenResult instead of throwing, so that the revocation of a replayed family is committed although the client receives an error.

  • Method Details

    • issueForCode

      @Transactional public OAuthTokenService.TokenResult issueForCode(OAuthRequestStore.CodeGrant grant)
      Creates the family of a redeemed code and issues its first token pair. The code itself was checked and consumed by the caller.

    • refresh

      @Transactional public OAuthTokenService.TokenResult refresh(String refreshToken, String clientId, String resource, String scope)
      Rotates a refresh token.
      Parameters:
      refreshToken - the refresh token in clear text
      clientId - the client_id of the token request, which must be the family's client
      resource - the resource of the token request, or null
      scope - the scope of the token request, or null; it can never widen the family's scope
